blocks.text: Superfluidity is a property of fluids where they have zero viscosity or are frictionless. A substance exhibiting this property is superfluid. Superfluids flow without loss of kinetic energy. In the laboratory, superfluids form in some substances at cryogenic temperature, not much above absolute zero.
Superfluids can flow through incredibly narrow spaces without any resistance. They can defy gravity and flow upwards against it as shown in Fig. 5.24.

blocks.alt: On a black background a glass tube rises diagonally from the lower left to the upper right. Along its lower wall a glowing yellow-orange-red film of superfluid creeps up the tube against gravity, thick in the middle and thinning to a yellow thread at the top, with small yellow drops at its lower end.
blocks.caption: Figure 5.24: A superfluid creeping up a tube against gravity (original drawing after the photograph printed as the textbook's Figure 5.24).
